approval.cost: 'Most developers pay 0% revenue share on their first $1,000,000 USD in lifetime gross app revenue and 15% above that.' No submission/review fee is stated
approval.trigger: Public distribution requires Shopify approval: the distribution comparison lists 'Approval required: Yes' for public distribution vs 'No' for custom distribution; you 'need to submit it to Shopify's App Approval team and make sure it meets all requirements'. Requirements are identical whether the listing is visible or not: 'Shopify's app requirements are the same for both fully visible and limited visibility public apps. If you're planning to list your app on the Shopify App Store, then Shopify also reviews the content that you provided for your listing page.' Process and statuses: 'Your app must meet all requirements on the App Store review page before your app is reviewed. During the review process your app changes status: Draft, Submitted, Reviewed, and Published.' A public app starts in Draft (tested on development stores); you click 'Submit your app' and it moves to Submitted (email confirmation; you can Withdraw). 'If your app doesn't meet core requirements that prevent a reviewer from reviewing your app, then your app moves to the Paused status' with an email of required changes; you resubmit via 'Submit fixes'. Then a reviewer is assigned; if fixes need discussion it moves to Reviewed; approval moves it to Published. Custom distribution needs no approval but installs only on 'a single Shopify store, on multiple stores that belong to the same Plus organization, or on development stores', and 'Can't charge merchants through Shopify's app billing system'.
approval.wait: Not stated (no duration appears in the review-process documentation read)

blockers.detail: 'You can't change the distribution method after you select it. Compare the capabilities and requirements of each type before choosing.'
blockers.howToClear: Decide public vs custom before creating the app configuration.
blockers.title: Distribution is a one-way door

blockers.detail: 'Use expiring offline access tokens for public apps that call the GraphQL Admin API.' 'Non-expiring offline tokens grant permanent access until the app is uninstalled or the secret is revoked. New public apps already can't use them for GraphQL Admin API requests, and existing public apps can't after January 1, 2027.' 'Public apps must use expiring offline access tokens for GraphQL Admin API requests by January 1, 2027. This doesn't apply to custom apps or apps created by merchants.'
blockers.howToClear: Request expiring=1 from the start and build the refresh loop; a 'store the token once, use forever' design is no longer viable for public apps.
blockers.title: Expiring-token migration deadline (January 1, 2027)

blockers.detail: 'Don't do the two at the same time for the same store. Acquiring a token and refreshing one each retire the other's result, so one of the two tokens your app receives is already invalid when it arrives.' Acquiring a fresh token via token exchange or the code grant immediately retires all other refresh tokens for that app+store. The presented refresh token 'stays usable until the earliest of: your app uses the newer refresh token; your app acquires a new token; 30 days after your app first used that token to refresh; the original 90-day expiry'. 'Shopify automatically retires your previous expiring offline token as your app acquires or refreshes tokens... Retired access tokens stay valid until their expires_in duration ends so in-progress requests can complete.' Shopify keeps 'one current expiring offline token per app and store'.
blockers.howToClear: Serialize token acquisition and refresh per store, and always persist the newest token pair.
blockers.title: Refresh races

flavor.recommended: A public-distribution app using Shopify managed installation + token exchange if embedded, or the authorization code grant if standalone; offline access tokens in their expiring form
flavor.why: The object is an 'app' created in Shopify's Dev Dashboard, identified by a client ID and client secret; the credential it obtains is an access token sent in the X-Shopify-Access-Token header ('Your app obtains a token through an authorization flow called a grant'). Three grants exist: token exchange (embedded apps exchange an App Bridge ID token for an access token with no merchant redirect), authorization code grant (standalone/API-only apps: 'redirect the merchant to Shopify, get their approval, and exchange a code for an access token'), and client credentials (own-organization stores only). Under managed installation, 'Shopify installs your app and updates its access scopes without calling your app. You declare the scopes your app needs in its shopify.app.toml configuration file and push it to Shopify, which then handles the merchant's approval.' Offline tokens 'persist across sessions and cover most app work, including background tasks such as webhooks and scheduled jobs'; online tokens are per-staff-member ('Request them when your app needs to respect an individual user's permission level'), selected in the code grant with grant_options[]=per-user.

name: Shopify
nuances: Refresh behavior (stated): 'Every refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Store both securely, and use the new refresh token in the next refresh request.' And: 'Read the expires_in value from the token response rather than hard-coding a duration, so your app keeps working if a lifetime changes.'

Online-token traps: 'if your app requests online access and isn't yet installed on the store, the user installing it must have every scope your app requires, or the installation fails', and 'Logging out revokes every online token minted during that web session, not just the current one'. The token response carries an associated_user object and associated_user_scope (the intersection of app scopes and that user's permissions); cache per user.

Scope quirks: 'Any permission to write a resource includes permission to read it, so request the write scope only when your app needs both.' Scopes declared in the TOML scopes field 'can't be requested dynamically'; only optional_scopes can be requested later (via the App Bridge Scopes API or a standalone request URL), and optional scopes can also be given back via dynamic scope revocation. Some scopes touch protected customer data, which 'places additional requirements on your app'.

'You can rotate your app's client secret, which invalidates access tokens tied to the old secret and requires every store's token to be refreshed.' Uninstall ends everything: 'a merchant uninstalling your app, or you revoking the client secret, ends all of a token's access. Requests then return 401.' ID-token handling: an expired/invalid ID token makes token exchange fail with 400 Bad Request; fetch a fresh ID token from App Bridge per exchange ('ID tokens are short-lived, so request one per exchange instead of caching it').

Legacy paths closing: apps created directly in the Shopify admin with pre-generated tokens 'can no longer be created'; private apps were deprecated in January 2022 and auto-migrated to custom apps; unpublished apps (public apps with no approval) were deprecated December 9, 2019. There is no longer a no-review route to many merchants.
prerequisites: A Shopify Partner/Dev account and a development store for testing
The distribution decision made before app creation (it cannot be changed)
A token store designed for expiring offline tokens (rotation, per-store serialization)

steps.detail: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard; obtain the client ID and client secret (keep the secret server-side). Select the distribution method (public vs custom); it cannot be changed later.
steps.title: Create the app; choose distribution

steps.detail: Declare the scopes your app needs (plus any optional_scopes) in shopify.app.toml and deploy/push the configuration to Shopify. Under managed installation Shopify handles the merchant's approval for declared scopes without calling your app. Test on a development store before submitting for review.
steps.title: Declare scopes in shopify.app.toml; push

steps.detail: Embedded: the merchant installs from the App Store/install link and Shopify presents its approval prompt for the declared scopes. On each embedded request, take the ID token from App Bridge and POST to https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token with client_id, client_secret, grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, subject_token, subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, requested_token_type (offline by default), and expiring=1 for an expiring offline token.
steps.title: Merchant installs; exchange the ID token

steps.detail: Redirect the merchant to https://{shop}/admin/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&scope=...&redirect_uri=...&state={nonce}&grant_options[]={access_mode} (per-user for an online token; omit for offline). Validate the state nonce and HMAC on the callback. POST the code to /admin/oauth/access_token with client_id, client_secret, code, and expiring=1 if you requested an offline token and want the expiring variant.
steps.title: Standalone alternative: authorization code grant

steps.detail: Call the GraphQL Admin API with the access token in the X-Shopify-Access-Token header. For expiring offline tokens, store the refresh token and refresh before the 1-hour expiry; every refresh returns a new pair, and acquiring or refreshing retires the other's result, so serialize per store.
steps.title: Call the Admin API; refresh expiring tokens

steps.detail: Prepare the listing and submit: Draft > Submitted (email confirmation) > possibly Paused (fix and 'Submit fixes') > Reviewed > Published. Shopify also reviews your listing page content if you list on the App Store.
steps.title: Submit for App Store review (public distribution)

tagline: A real OAuth program with a hard edge: public distribution needs Shopify's App Approval review, the distribution choice is irreversible, and public apps must move to expiring offline tokens (1-hour access, 90-day refresh) for the GraphQL Admin API by January 1, 2027.
